item.title: Embattled Mayfield approaches crucial General Meeting as Embark presses for Board spill
item.description: ASX listed Mayfield Childcare’s General Meeting for Shareholders, convened in the wake of majority shareholder Embark Early Education’s request, is scheduled to take place on 25 November, 2026 at 2:00pm AEDT and will see resolutions to remove three Mayfield Directors put to shareholders to vote.

item.title: Carmel Tebbutt appointed as first female Chair of NESA Board
item.description: The NSW Department of Education has announced the former NSW Deputy Premier and Education Minister Carmel Tebbutt has been appointed as the next Chair of the NSW Education Standards Authority Board, becoming the first woman to chair the NESA Board. The appointment takes effect from 1 January 2027.
item.content:encoded: The NSW Department of Education has announced the former NSW Deputy Premier and Education Minister Carmel Tebbutt has been appointed as the next Chair of the NSW Education Standards Authority Board, becoming the first woman to chair the NESA Board. The appointment takes effect from 1 January 2027.

item.title: Small NSW services face staffing squeeze as "working towards" ECT rule ends 1 January
item.description: From 1 January 2027, educators working towards an approved early childhood teaching qualification will no longer automatically be counted as early childhood teachers (ECTs) in NSW centre-based services educating and caring for 29 children or fewer, from 1 January 2027.

item.title: How play-based learning supports children's social and emotional development
item.description: Play is not just a fun activity in children's lives. It helps children to learn how to establish relationships, to observe and learn about emotions, and the abilities needed to engage in everyday social encounters.

item.title: How can providers prepare for new supervision rules due to come into force next year?
item.description: Approved providers have another set of obligations to plan for, after education ministers agreed that meeting ratios will not, on its own, show children are adequately supervised, as The Sector reported in 'Meeting ratios won't be enough'. The Department of Education published the details on 18 November, but the legislation and guidance behind them are not expected until 2027.
